newsitem.title: USA: USWC prods steady on subdued news, ample diesels.
newsitem.headline: USWC prods steady on subdued news, ample diesels.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast products stayed at levels seen earlier Thursday, with news from Iraq faded and distillate stocks seen at normal levels compared to the rest of the country.

The U.S. government's Energy Information Administration (EIA) showed PADD 5 West Coast distillate stocks at 10.8 million barrels last week, just 900,000 barrels below levels seen last year at this time.
Meanwhile, nationwide, distillates were seen a steep 21 million off 1995 for the same period.

Prices for CARB-grade diesel in Los Angeles were assessed three cents higher than the beginning of the week, with traders attributing firmness to problems at Mobil's large gas-making unit in Torrance, Calif..
The unit was rumoured to be resuming service early Friday.
However, traders said a large gas-making unit at Chevron's Los Angeles refinery could shut for maintenance late this week, though a spokeswoman denied the rumor.
Growing diesel consumption also firmed prices on the week, as California harvesting is due to increase in early October.
